note: The programme's own assessment of each epic's exit gate (from the PRD), written by hand. A gate may be 'met' only if every evidence path exists; the release decision refuses an unevidenced 'met'. 'partially_met' is listed as a caveat, 'not_met' and 'not_measured' block.

gates.gate: inventory, baseline and status observer work before any epic is marked in progress
at least one current-engine independent evaluation is accurately run or explicitly blocked, with scoring and leakage instrumentation; no target F1 claimed
gates.note: A valid run exists (F1 0.040). No target is claimed and the sealed holdout was not used.

gates.gate: concrete missed real-code vulnerabilities recovered with causal explanations and matched safe controls; deterministic completion under analysis budgets
gates.note: No missed vulnerability from the independent population was shown to be recovered. The dataflow and IR work was measured on fixtures; the baseline run already contains it, so its effect on real code has no before measurement. 272 of 278 scored entries are still missed.

gates.gate: every supported patch route gives the same evidence-based verification result, behavioural regressions are caught, no write occurs when mandatory verification fails
gates.note: One declared gap still accepts an unsafe fix (1 of 15) and 3 of 8 safe fixes are refused; both are listed in the benchmark.

gates.gate: real-world-context examples are measurable, high-confidence findings have reproducible proof, safe paths do not become false positives, unknowns are not promoted
gates.note: Measurable and proof-backed, but the cases are synthetic and author-labelled, two safe routes become false positives, and Flask is mostly unresolved.

gates.gate: cross-artifact evidence matches immutable identities, unknowns are preserved, no private runtime data leaks by default
gates.note: Runtime collection is off until a policy file enables it; records from another build corroborate nothing. Several pieces are library code, not default scan behaviour.

gates.gate: bounded scans, trustworthy scan-health semantics, no new uncontrolled egress or execution, measured performance benefit
gates.note: Scans are bounded and containment is measured, but the measured benefit (1.72 times for one changed file) is under the 2 times aspiration and the 829-file class never completes its deep analysis.

gates.gate: independent offline verification, truthful compliance and coverage claims, privacy safe, one lineage from code and tests to the executive and audit report
gates.note: Shown on the demo project; the default scan does not assemble or sign a package. Provenance attribution is below its 95 percent target.
